title: Global tech policymakers agree to embrace AI in science
key_facts: The United States and 15 other countries are to release a joint statement on Sunday 4 Oct 2026 at the Science and Technology in Society Forum in Kyoto, Japan.
The statement is titled the 'Kyoto Vision for a Golden Age of Science'; NBC News saw it in advance.

It encourages research that integrates AI (called 'super intelligence' after a recent Trump executive order renaming the technology) and welcomes the field of metascience, the study of the scientific process itself.
Michael Kratsios, head of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy, led the statement; ministers from Japan, Korea, the UK and the UAE are among the endorsers.
Kratsios's planned remarks describe robot-run laboratories and AI systems designing and analysing experiments at superhuman speed.

The statement also calls public trust the bedrock of science; critics such as Gretchen Goldman of the Union of Concerned Scientists say the administration has undermined trust through research funding cuts, including a proposed roughly 50 percent cut to the National Science Foundation in the 2027 budget.
It follows the 'White House Accord on Super Intelligence', a voluntary four-part safety approach agreed with tech executives days earlier, and Kratsios's Genesis Mission on AI-accelerated discovery.
quote_evidence: The United States on Sunday will release a joint statement with 15 other countries describing a shared vision for a “golden age of science” that embraces the potential of artificial intelligence.

Michael Kratsios, head of the White House’s Office of Science and Technology Policy, spearheaded the vision statement, which also says the participating countries welcome the “growing field of metascience,”
“It’s hard to take seriously any promises of increased trust and transparency when you look at the actions they’ve taken,” Goldman said.
why_it_matters_hint: Sixteen governments are putting AI-driven research and metascience into a shared science agenda, while US critics point to deep funding cuts at home.
notes: Single-outlet advance report of a statement seen by NBC before release; written as expected, not as released.
